item.title: Florida drops impressive offensive performance to pull off massive win over No. 4 Ole Miss
item.description: The Florida Gators stunned No. 4 Ole Miss in the Swamp with a dominant ground game as two running backs each rushed for over 100 yards in the win.
item.content:encoded:
After one of the most emotionally intense games of the season against their former coach Lane Kiffin and LSU, Ole Miss traveled down to the Swamp to take on the Florida Gators.

Sure, the intensity going into the game was nothing like the week before, but Florida was always going to be a challenge, coming in as the No. 21 team in the nation, with Ole Miss showing up in Gainesville at No. 4.

However, in the early going, it was all Florida.

JON SUMRALL SHARES HILARIOUS RESPONSE TO HEARING HIS FLORIDA TEAM IS FAVORED AGAINST OLE MISS

Gators running back Jadan Baugh opened the scoring with a short run to the end zone. Kicker Patrick Durkin tacked on the extra point and hung another three points on the board with a field goal later in the quarter.

Ole Miss finally got their zero off the board with a field goal early in the second quarter and another late.

FLORIDA GATORS, OLE MISS REBELS FIND THEMSELVES IN GOOD OLD-FASHIONED 'RESPECT OFF' AHEAD OF SATURDAY'S GAME

Unfortunately for Ole Miss, those two field goals sandwiched another rushing touchdown for Baugh, and the Gators took a 17-6 lead to the locker room at halftime.

The second half is when the offense really started to heat up.

Ole Miss signal caller Trinidad Chambliss scored a rushing touchdown on the team's first drive of the half. However, Florida answered right back with a rushing touchdown from running back Duke Clark.

It was all about the ground game. Florida posted 302 rushing yards, with both Baugh and Clark rushing for over 100 yards apiece, making it the first time two Gators have done that in the same game since 2022.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Florida led the entire game and really pulled away in the fourth quarter, which saw the lone passing touchdown of their seven trips to the red zone on the day.

The Gators offense has been impressive, putting up more than 50 points in all but one game this season, but this was one that is really going to get them some attention ...

That one game where they failed to hit the 50-point mark? That was last weekend against Auburn, in which they scored a paltry 44 points.

Florida hadn't beaten a top-5 team since a win over Georgia in 2020, and there's no doubt that this win is going to shake up the rankings.

Next, the Gators will turn their attention to the No. 19 Missouri Tigers, while Ole Miss will look to bounce back in a couple of weeks against Vanderbilt.

item.title: Enes Freedom rips Cheryl Reeve for saying women's sports advocates 'don’t want transgender people to exist'
item.description: Enes Kanter Freedom called on Cheryl Reeve to step down after the Lynx coach said the transgender athletes debate targets trans people's existence.
item.content:encoded:
Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom pushed back against Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve after she claimed the debate over transgender athletes is part of a broader effort by critics who "don’t want transgender people to exist."

Freedom responded to Reeve in a social media post Saturday, rejecting her characterization of those advocating to keep biological males out of women’s sports.

"Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve should step down immediately. You can’t lead women’s basketball while refusing to stand up for women’s sports. Can someone, for the love of God, please explain to her that: Protecting women’s sports is not an attack on anyone’s existence, nor does it erase a community. Coach, if you truly mean what you just said, then put your hypocrisy aside and prove it by drafting me in the 2027 WNBA Draft," Freedom wrote.

LYNX COACH CHERYL REEVE VOICES SUPPORT FOR THE TRANS COMMUNITY AGAIN AFTER REGULAR SEASON FINALE VS FEVER

Reeve made the remarks after the Lynx closed the regular season with an 86-66 victory over the Indiana Fever at Target Center Thursday. The game was accompanied by competing demonstrations outside the arena over transgender participation in women’s sports.

"I think that’s probably one of the more meaningful things that would mark the season for me," Reeve said. "It’s that the transgender community is one that deserves our support, and what is happening in the name of some issues of transgender in sports — it’s really an attack on all transgender community. They don’t want transgender people to exist."

Reeve said the reaction she received after wearing a "Trans Kids Belong" shirt during a nationally televised Aug. 2 game against Indiana made the gesture one of the most meaningful moments of her season.

"The amount of communication of people who were affected by something as simple as wearing a T-shirt in support of them and helping them be seen — with the platform that we have in professional sports, it was a small gesture by me," Reeve said. "It’s something I believe in, obviously, wholeheartedly."

"If I could have helped just one to feel differently about themselves, because for the transgender community this really is about life and death for them," she continued. "The number of parents of transgender kids that I heard from and how it helped them and their families, it helped their child think differently about themselves and that there is someone in our position, like we have as a leader. To know that there are people out there that believe in them, that they belong."

The comments marked at least the fourth time Reeve addressed the transgender issue during a WNBA media availability this season.

WNBA COMMISSIONER CATHY ENGELBERT SENDS TRANS INCLUSION MEMO AFTER ENES FREEDOM, ROYCE WHITE ANNOUNCEMENTS

Reeve initially spoke about it following Supreme Court rulings that upheld state laws protecting women’s and girls’ sports. She later defended transgender participation before the Lynx’s first home game against the Fever, saying that "every kid has a right to sports" while acknowledging that eligibility becomes more complicated after puberty.

The four-time WNBA champion coach also spoke privately with Fever guard Sophie Cunningham before their Aug. 2 matchup. Cunningham previously said she wanted to protect girls who should not have to compete against or share locker rooms with biological males, while emphasizing that she did not harbor hatred toward transgender people.

"I think that I am here to extend love," Cunningham said. "But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men."

Freedom inserted himself into the WNBA’s transgender debate in August by announcing that he intended to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft under the name "Enisa Freedom." He said the move was designed to test the league’s eligibility standards, which state that only women may play in the WNBA but do not publicly define eligibility through biological sex.

ENES KANTER FREEDOM OPENS UP ON CONFRONTATION WITH NATASHA CLOUD THAT LED TO EJECTION, WNBA PURSUIT

The former NBA center has repeatedly maintained that he is raising the issue seriously and is not attempting to demean transgender people.

"I’m not here to mock, make fun of, or disrespect any group or anyone’s personal decisions," Freedom wrote in an earlier statement. "What I’m trying to do is bigger than clicks or attention."

Freedom also publicly separated his campaign from the conduct of other former male basketball players who joined the WNBA draft effort, saying his goal had "never been publicity, political theater, cheap attention, or stunts."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Former NBA player Royce White also responded to Reeve’s latest remarks, but took a distinctly different approach from Freedom. While Freedom offered a direct rebuttal to Reeve’s characterization of women’s-sports advocates, White issued an overtly satirical statement promoting his female alter ego, "Roysha."

"I appreciate Coach Reeve’s sentiment toward Transgenders," White wrote. "In these increasingly polarized times, it appears a potential source of cultural common ground has emerged ... Kweeen Roysha! Pay is the perfect blend of MAGA and mainstream. I think there’s a real opportunity to create a bridge, because a lot of conservatives nationwide would like to see Roysha play in the WNBA. The Minnesota Lynx would be a perfect home as the new transgender capital of America."

The WNBA previously said there were no immediate transgender eligibility matters affecting the league and condemned what it called "bad-faith efforts" to demean or marginalize others. The league has never had a transgender woman play on a roster. Its collective bargaining agreement states that "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA" but does not publicly provide a more detailed definition based on biological sex.

Commissioner Cathy Engelbert said during the season that the league would continue discussions with team leaders and the players’ union while treating competitive integrity, fairness and inclusion as priorities.

item.title: Pope Leo draws staggering 800,000 faithful to heart of Paris for massive outdoor Mass
item.description: Pope Leo XIV drew an estimated 800,000 to Place de la Concorde for a historic open-air Mass, urging French Catholics to share their faith openly.
item.content:encoded:
Pope Leo XIV drew an estimated 800,000 people into the heart of Paris on Saturday for a massive open-air Mass, filling one of the French republic’s most storied public squares as he urged Catholics to openly share their faith in an "increasingly secularized society."

Flag-waving crowds packed the Champs-Élysées and Place de la Concorde as the American pope traveled roughly 1.2 miles through central Paris in the popemobile before celebrating Mass.

The Vatican estimated attendance at 800,000, roughly 200,000 more people than had registered in advance.

People of faith gathered in the streets, with families lifting babies and young children toward the popemobile as Leo made his way through the French capital.

POPE LEO XIV RECEIVES 'SYMBOLIC’ SPHERE IN CHARITY'S PUSH FOR AI TO 'PROTECT HUMAN DIGNITY'

"Seeing you gathered here," Leo told worshippers, he was looking upon the "heirs of France’s long and beautiful history of faith," according to Vatican News.

The pope called on French Catholics not to keep that rich inheritance to themselves.

FROM DISNEY MAGIC TO ANCIENT FAITH: DAVID HENRIE ON WHY GEN Z IS FLOCKING TO CHURCH

"Let it overflow, so that those you meet may be refreshed and their thirst satisfied," Leo said. "From this beautiful city of Paris, I pray fervently that the living water of the Holy Spirit may flow throughout France."

The setting carried particular resonance in a country known for its strict tradition of secularism.

AMERICAN BISHOP ROBERT BARRON CALLS OUT ST. PAUL'S CATHEDRAL IN UK OVER NIGHTCLUB PARTNERSHIP

It is notable that the Place de la Concorde was an execution ground during the French Revolution, where devoutly Catholic King Louis XVI and Queen Marie Antoinette were guillotined. Today, the square is closely associated with the French republic and regularly hosts Bastille Day celebrations.

The decision to celebrate a papal Mass there drew criticism from supporters of France’s strict separation of church and state, who argued another site would have been more appropriate.

The images also offered a striking contrast with another massive Paris spectacle just two years earlier.

The 2024 Summer Olympics opening ceremony drew worldwide controversy over a tableau featuring drag performers that Christian leaders and other critics said mocked Christianity.

POLL FINDS SHARP RISE IN YOUNG MEN CALLING RELIGION 'VERY IMPORTANT'

The French Bishops’ Conference said at the time that the ceremony "included scenes of mockery and derision of Christianity," adding that Christians around the world had been "hurt by the outrageousness and provocation of certain scenes."

The tableau was widely interpreted by critics as a parody of Leonardo da Vinci’s "The Last Supper," though Olympics organizers disputed that interpretation.

Leo’s visit comes as France experiences a notable increase in adult conversions even as the country continues a decades-long decline in overall Catholic participation.

Annual adult baptisms in France have tripled since 2016, reaching 13,000 this year, according to The Associated Press. Overall baptisms, however, have fallen sharply over the longer term, from 513,000 in 1980 to 186,000 in 2024.

YOUNG MEN ARE RETURNING TO CHURCH — AND IT COULD RESHAPE AMERICA’S FUTURE

Leo thanked French families, young people, catechumens and new Christians for bearing witness to their faith in what he described as an "increasingly secularized society," according to Vatican News.

The scale of the pope’s reception was already apparent the night before the Mass as some 80,000 young people packed France’s national stadium Friday for a vigil featuring fireworks and a theatrical retelling of the country’s Catholic history.

"Thank you for your courage! Thank you for your presence," Leo told them in French. "Thank you for your faith. You are the saints of France!"

At Saturday’s Mass, Leo invoked France’s Catholic heritage and drew on the biblical image of "living water," telling worshippers that Jesus Christ could satisfy humanity’s desire for "life, truth, unity, peace, communion, and happiness."

He also invoked French Catholic saints including Irenaeus, Martin and Francis de Sales while praising those who continue to work for "life, the family, truth, peace, fraternity and justice."

The sea of people rivaled some of the largest public celebrations to fill the Champs-Élysées in recent decades, including France’s World Cup victories in 1998 and 2018, according to the AP.

Leo’s four-day trip to France began Friday with a visit to the restored Notre Dame Cathedral, the first by a pope since the devastating 2019 fire.

He traveled Saturday night to Lourdes, one of the Catholic Church’s most visited pilgrimage sites.

item.title: Ben Affleck admits his teenager roasted his dating history while at dinner
item.description: Ben Affleck revealed on "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" that his 17-year-old roasted his relationship history at dinner, proving he's not the cool dad.
item.content:encoded:
Ben Affleck is getting real about being a parent to teenagers, and how he can sometimes be the butt of a joke.

During a recent interview on "Jimmy Kimmel Live!," the 54-year-old actor got candid about what it's like parenting teenagers, saying he never could have imagined he "wouldn't be the cool dad."

"I'll give you an example. My kids are talking at dinner, and they'll talk about their friends and the drama and the relationships and I have some lived experience I think that's worth sharing, some lessons … these are the kind of things we give to our children."

He then recalled trying to give his kids advice about a relationship, when "the 17-year-old just turns to me and goes, 'Oh, like you're the expert on relationships?'"

JENNIFER GARNER SAYS DIVORCE FROM BEN AFFLECK CAUSED 'UPHEAVAL' THAT KEPT HER FROM WORKING FOR YEARS

Affleck shares three children with his ex-wife, Jennifer Garner, including Violet, 20, Fin, 17, and Samuel, 14.

He and Garner were married for over 10 years before deciding to separate in 2015, later finalizing their divorce in 2018. Aside from Garner, Affleck has been in many high-profile relationships, including "Saturday Night Live's" Lindsay Shookus and Playboy model Shauna Sexton.

The "Good Will Hunting Star" then made waves in 2019 when he was spotted with actress Ana de Armas, who he dated from late 2019 until early 2021, after which he reconnected with his former fiancé, Jennifer Lopez.

Lopez and Affleck initially dated from 2002 to 2004 and reconnected in April 2021. They went Instagram official in July 2021, were engaged by April 2022 and got married that July.

"We really live our lives in a way we can be proud of and our kids can be proud of you," she wrote in her newsletter at the time. "We're just operating from a place of love and respect for everyone in our lives and that is very important to us. We know what the truth is [and] we hold it sacred."

After just over two years of marriage, Lopez filed for divorce in August 2024.

When speaking to host Jimmy Kimmel, Affleck shared that Garner was approached to play his love interest in his newest film, "Animals," but she passed on the opportunity.

"Jen was like, ‘Great, but no, I’m not gonna play your wife in a movie,'" he said. "[It’s] probably for the best. That lesson has been learned."

After Garner turned him down, Affleck turned to Kerry Washington, who accepted the role. The movie, which Affleck also directed and co-wrote, follows the story of the husband and wife duo who do whatever it takes to pay their son's ransom.

item.title: Civilian detained after 'violently engaging' security personnel at Florida Air Force base: report
item.description: A civilian reportedly breached MacDill Air Force Base's perimeter and violently engaged security personnel, prompting the closure of the Dale Mabry Gate.
item.content:encoded:
A civilian assailant was detained outside MacDill Air Force Base in Florida on Saturday after the person "violently engaged" security personnel, according to reports, citing the 6th Air Refueling Wing Public Affairs Office.

The civilian breached the perimeter of the Tampa base around 1 p.m. Saturday and got into a violent argument with security, leaving one officer and the civilian with non-life-threatening injuries, according to FOX 13 and WTSP-TV. 

"The Dale Mabry Gate is currently closed to inbound and outbound traffic until further notice," the base posted on Facebook around 2:30 p.m. "Please plan accordingly and avoid the Dale Mabry Gate area until further notice."

The investigation is ongoing.

The base didn’t specify what led to the attack.

The headquarters of U.S. Central Command are located at the base.

item.title: Texas dropped some celebrations against Tennessee that were about as unhinged as they come
item.description: Colin Simmons and Raleek Brown drew penalties and viral attention with bizarre below-the-belt celebrations during the Texas Longhorns' game at Tennessee.
item.content:encoded:
As anticipated, there was no game on Saturday's college football slate, as the Texas Longhorns made their trip to Knoxville to face the Tennessee Volunteers. Emotions were bound to be high, and with that often comes some big celebrations.

That said, no one was prepared for what some Longhorns had up their sleeves ... and in their pants.

Of course, over-the-top celebrations are nothing new, but let's see what the Longhorns were throwing down on Saturday.

NO. 1 TEXAS ESCAPES TENNESSEE WITH THRILLING SEC VICTORY AS PRESIDENT TRUMP WATCHES ON FROM NEYLAND STADIUM

Let's start with junior edge rusher Colin Simmons, who hauled down a scrambling Faizon Brandon for a big, 16-yard loss deep in their own end of the field.

Hey, that's a big play. Go ahead and do a little celebrating, big guy.

...Alright, maybe not that one.

That's the kind of celebration you dust off to make your buddies laugh during a Thanksgiving Day pickup game in the backyard after a couple of Michelob Ultras. Not when you're in the midst of a huge ranked matchup.

KYLE JUSZCZYK RESPONDS TO BEER FINE BY EXPLAINING IN DETAIL HIS CELEBRATION IS ABOUT HIS NICKNAME – JUICE

The celebration hurt the team — and not just from a reputational perspective — as Simmons was handed a penalty for "simulating using the restroom," which meant that the sack resulted in just a single-yard loss.

Of course, social media went nuts.

And, as if this all wasn't crazy enough, Jemele Hill, winner of the 2021 OutKick Woke All-Star Challenge, wrote something that made me laugh, and for the reason it was intended.

We give credit where it's due around here.

Of course, Simmons apologized, but did so using possibly the worst phrasing given the situation.

We get what he meant...

SEC CROWD GREETS TRUMP WITH MASSIVE CHEERS AHEAD OF TENNESSEE-TEXAS SHOWDOWN

Well, at least that was the end of south-of-the-equator celebrations we got from the Longhorns on Saturday. It's not like anyone trotted into the end zone for a game-winning touchdown, then popped their leg up like Captain Morgan, swiped their hand across their crotch, pretended to sniff it, and then passed out or anything. That would be insane.

... Wait, running back Raleek Brown did what?

If this is what they do in a stadium in front of thousands of people, what kind of celebrations are they doing elsewhere?!

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

A moment like this meant that the admin for the DUDE Wipes X account sprang into action to do what they'd taken an oath to do.

I just can't get over that both of those happened in the same game. You'd think after the first incident someone would've said, "Hey, fellas, let's steer clear of any celebrations that might stray into the groin-al region."

Nope.

Man, McConaughey is going to need to have a word with the team about this.

That's not alright ... alright, alright.

item.title: Costco membership offers hidden savings beyond groceries: 5 perks to know
item.description: Costco executive membership perks extend far beyond bulk groceries, with hidden savings on gas, travel packages, gift cards and tire maintenance.
item.content:encoded:
A Costco membership is best known for bulk groceries, the $1.50 hot dog combo and towering packs of paper goods, but some of the biggest savings can happen well beyond the winding checkout lines.

From travel and gas to gift cards, optical services and warranty coverage, Costco members can access a range of discounts and services, according to the company’s website and news reports.

Here are five lesser-known ways shoppers can stretch their Costco membership outside of the warehouse aisles.

WEALTHY AMERICANS CHOOSE ONE GROCERY STORE CHAIN OVER RIVALS, SURVEY FINDS

Buying Costco gas can help households offset the annual membership free, according to Money Talks News. It often costs less than competitors, though the actual savings vary by location and driving habits, according to the outlet.

An additional perk is that Costco members can check local gas prices and station hours through the Costco app before heading to the pump.

And another secret at the pump is that the warehouse’s long hoses also allow drivers to fuel up from either side of their vehicle. "Whether your gas tank is on the left or right side of your car, you can choose the shortest line," Costco's website reads.

COSTCO FOOD COURT ITEM PACKS MORE PROTEIN THAN ANYTHING ELSE ON THE MENU, BUT THERE'S A CATCH

Upgrading from Costco's annual $65 membership to the $130 Executive membership includes an annual 2% reward — up to $1,250 — on certain purchases.

Since the upgrade costs $65 more than a Gold Star membership, shoppers would need about $3,250 in qualifying annual spending to cover the added upgrade cost.

COSTCO BRINGS BACK A FAN-FAVORITE FOOD COURT TREAT AFTER YEARS OFF THE MENU

Executive members also receive earlier warehouse access, beginning at 9 a.m. at many locations, plus additional discounts on select Costco Services.

Costco Travel lets members book vacation packages, cruises, hotels and rental cars through Costco. Executive members can also earn their 2% annual reward on qualifying travel purchases, though the reward is credited after the trip is completed.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

One member who booked a Costa Rica trip reported getting a $200 Shop Card after returning, paying for more than three years of membership, Money Talk News Reported.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Costco sells gift cards for a variety of activities, from theme park tickets to city exploration passes, according to its website, for a discounted price.

"Costco offers deals like two $50 gift cards for $79.99 or four $15 gift cards for $44.99," Linda Chavez, founder and CEO of Seniors Life Insurance Finder, told Real Simple. "These offers make stocking up on gift cards for Christmas or birthdays a breeze," she added. "Gift cards for movie theaters, theme parks, performances, activities and more are also available."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Costco shoppers who buy tires through its tire center receive free rotation, balancing, pressure checks and flat repairs for the life of those tires, according to Money Talks News.

Those services can add up over time, though shoppers should compare tire prices and available services locally before buying, the website noted.

item.title: Arch Manning does interview with Holly Rowe after controversy over AI slapping video comment
item.description: Arch Manning and Holly Rowe shared a cordial postgame interview after Texas' 20-17 win over Tennessee, weeks after the AI video controversy.
item.content:encoded:
Texas quarterback Arch Manning did a postgame interview with ESPN reporter Holly Rowe on Saturday, less than two weeks after apologizing for calling an AI-generated video that depicted her being slapped "hilarious."

Rowe interviewed Manning on the field after No. 1 Texas survived a late comeback attempt by No. 14 Tennessee to earn a 20-17 victory at Neyland Stadium.

"I know this was a hard-fought win. This was dramatic down the stretch, but that long drive, you guys punch it in, you go over, and you're hyping up your offensive line. How huge was that moment for you guys in this game?" Rowe asked.

NO. 1 TEXAS ESCAPES TENNESSEE WITH THRILLING SEC VICTORY AS PRESIDENT TRUMP WATCHES ON FROM NEYLAND STADIUM

"It was fun," Manning said. "I thought they battled the whole time. Shout out to our defense. Colin Simmons, that's a real player right there."

Rowe then asked Manning about the significance of winning at the stadium where his uncle, Peyton Manning, became a college football legend.

"He was terrific today. Your whole team was," Rowe said. "But I know a lot of people think this is a special day for your family. You made your own history out on this field today. What was that like for you, Arch?"

"It's not about me," Manning responded. "I didn't play very well, but our team played great. Defense played well. SEC road win, that's what it's all about."

Manning completed 14 of 19 passes for 201 yards and an interception. He was sacked six times as Texas finished with just 262 total yards and committed 11 penalties for 115 yards. The Longhorns’ defense recorded 10 sacks, including a program record-tying five by Simmons.

Rowe closed by asking Manning about the encouragement he offered Tennessee quarterback Faizon Brandon after the game.

TEXAS' STEVE SARKISAN'S FIRST INTERVIEW WITH HOLLY ROWE GOES OFF WITHOUT A HITCH AFTER VIRAL POSTGAME INCIDENT

"I just said keep going," Manning said. "He's a great player. I wish him all the best."

"Thanks so much," Rowe said.

"Thank you. Appreciate it," Manning responded.

The interview garnered mixed reactions on social media, with some praising the cordial nature of it despite the context, while others shared concerns that Manning's personality appears depleted after the controversy and subsequent apology.

ARCH MANNING ISSUES APOLOGY AFTER FACING HEAT FOR LAUGHING AT AI VIDEO OF STEVE SARKISIAN SLAPPING HOLLY ROWE

The exchange attracted additional attention because of the controversy that followed Texas’ dramatic 24-23 comeback win over Ohio State on Sept. 12.

After that game, Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian interrupted Rowe’s opening question, shouted, "Texas fight" and "Hook ’em," and walked away from the interview. An altered video subsequently circulated on social media that falsely showed Sarkisian slapping Rowe.

When Manning was asked about social media edits during a press conference two days later, he brought up the fabricated clip.

"I saw an AI edit of Sark’s interview," Manning said. "Y’all seen that one? That’s a good one. Of him slapping Holly Rowe. It’s hilarious."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Manning apologized the following day, acknowledging that there was "nothing funny about it" and that his comment had been hurtful.

"I specifically want to apologize to Holly Rowe for what she has personally had to deal with because of my comments," Manning wrote. "I have a ton of respect for her and appreciate her showing me grace in this moment. I need to do better and will be more thoughtful going forward."

Rowe publicly accepted the apology and revealed that she and Manning had spoken privately.

"Thank you Arch," Rowe wrote. "I appreciate our conversation about this — which will remain private. Apology accepted. We move forward with respect and kindness for one another."

Saturday’s interview appeared to reflect that sentiment, with Rowe praising Manning and the quarterback thanking her before they parted ways.

item.title: Arch Manning revels in cigar smoke: Texas leaves Neyland with win—and a warning for college football
item.description: Steve Sarkisian refused to apologize for how the Texas Longhorns won at Tennessee, noting they still have seven ranked opponents left to play.
item.content:encoded:
KNOXVILLE, TN - Cigar smoke was coming from the Texas locker room following their win over Tennessee on Saturday afternoon that came down to the final play.

The only offense that we really got on a consistent basis Saturday between Tennessee and Texas came when the Secret Service was clearing an area for President Trump to walk through while the national anthem was being played.

A slugfest of wacky proportions played out inside Neyland Stadium, with Arch Manning doing just enough to get his Longhorns out of Knoxville with the win.

SEC CROWD GREETS TRUMP WITH MASSIVE CHEERS AHEAD OF TENNESSEE-TEXAS SHOWDOWN

The entire morning was filled with anticipation, as the President would finally make his way from the airport to Tennessee's campus for what would turn out to be a first half appearance.

But, it was the Texas defense that showed up for the party with a reckoning on its mind, finishing with ten total sacks, which Steve Sarkisian said led to eight Tennessee players being helped out of the field in what turned out to be another physical SEC game.

TENNESSEE FANS EXCITED FOR TRUMP'S ATTENDANCE AT GAME VS TEXAS: 'I HOPE HE STAYS THE WHOLE GAME'

What's the biggest takeaway?

The Longhorns have the two-best wins in college football this season, after defeating Ohio State just fourteen days ago.

Steve Sarkisian, will not apologize for how his team wins, nor should he.

"For us, we’ve got more of these to go..We have 7 ranked opponents we have still yet to play..That's why I’m not gonna apologize for how we beat a top-15 team on the road, when others don’t even play them," Sarkisian said postgame.

We wondered how the Longhorns would react to a hostile environment, with over 100,000 fans starting to enter the gates in hopes of taking advantage of alcoholic beverages that were 50% off , thanks to the Tennessee athletic department enticing fans to enter the stadium before traffic got out of hand due to Trump's arrival.

That answer was provided on the defensive side of the ball for Texas throughout the entire game, as Tennessee quarterback Faizon Brandon scrambled for his life on what felt like every other play for the Vols.

DONALD TRUMP ADDS POLITICAL STAKES, ANTICIPATION AND POTENTIAL SIDELINE CHAOS TO TEXAS-TENNESSEE SHOWDOWN

Heck, Texas' Colin Simmons had five sacks on the day, making life extremely difficult for the Vols freshman QB.

If you were under the impression that this Steve Sarkisian led football team wasn’t prepared for their first road trip of the season, you were sorely mistaken. There were some that wrote about how this physical test on the road would be to their detriment.

NO. 1 TEXAS ESCAPES TENNESSEE WITH THRILLING SEC VICTORY AS PRESIDENT TRUMP WATCHES ON FROM NEYLAND STADIUM

I guess they aren't watching the same Texas team. This group continues to find ways to win, in the most difficult era of college football. Whether it was on the final play of the game, or holding off an offense on the last series, the Longhorns have figured it out early this season.

Sure, he might have only thrown for 127 yards in the first half, taking a 10-3 lead into halftime. But, that didn’t stop him from finding pockets of success in the second half, which kept his team ahead when the final whistle blew.

And yes, Manning only finished the game with 201 yards passing with zero touchdowns, but he put Texas in a position to win once again.

Whether it was Cam Coleman or Ryan Wingo, Tennessee did not seem to have an answer for the talented pair on a consistent basis, which came back to bite the Vols during the second half.

Seven total sacks for the Texas defense also kept the Vols offense in check for a majority of the game.

This was the first road test, and they passed. At the end of the day, when Texas boards the plane home for Austin, that's all that matters for this team.

We can talk about some of the sloppy offensive line play, or the weird unsportsmanlike penalty on Colin Simmons, but that's just noise right now.

What we witnessed on Saturday afternoon was two teams who are still working out the glitches. The problem for Tennessee is that they do not have a veteran starter, while Arch Manning is finding different ways to get his squad into the end zone.

All the while, Texas once again proved they might be the best overall team in college football in one of the hardest places to play in this sport.

As the equipment staff began loading the truck for its ride back to Texas, you can hear the noise coming from inside the Longhorns locker room.

"We're the real UT, so they can stop talking," one player said aloud.

On Saturday afternoon in Knoxville, this Texas team once again proved it could find another way to win.

But, in the end, it still came down to their defense. Just as it did against Ohio State.

You don't rack up 12 sacks on an SEC opponent without having a stellar group on that side of the ball. Maybe we should be talking more about the unit who has provided four wins on the season, with two against Top-15 teams.

It's easy to get lost in Arch. We might wanna get used to this defense.

item.title: Tigers legend Justin Verlander leaves mound in tears after daughter surprises him during final career start
item.description: A.J. Hinch sent Genevieve Verlander sprinting to the mound to pull her dad from his final career start, sparking an emotional scene at Comerica Park.
item.content:encoded:
Who said there is no crying in baseball?

Justin Verlander’s final start of his illustrious career brought out all the emotions, including some tears from the 42-year-old. Detroit Tigers manager A.J. Hinch came out of the dugout to pull the legendary starter after 5 1/3 innings of two-run ball in the Tigers’ 4-3 win over the Pittsburgh Pirates on Saturday but didn’t walk to the mound.

Hinch instead brought out someone special to Verlander to remove him from his last start: his daughter, Genevieve.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Genevieve came sprinting out of her seat and gave her dad a hug by the pitcher’s mound. Verlander embraced his daughter for more than 15 seconds as his body shook with emotion and the tears began to flow. The emotional Verlander then composed himself as he hugged his infielders one final time.

After hugging his teammates, he walked off the mound hand-in-hand with his daughter as the raucous Tigers crowd gave their longtime ace a rousing ovation.

Before greeting his teammates, he hugged his wife, Kate Upton, who was holding their second child. The 2011 American League MVP then high-fived all of his teammates and coaches, who had all come out of the dugout, before walking down the dugout steps with Upton and Genevieve.

TIGERS LEGEND JUSTIN VERLANDER'S FINAL CAREER START SIGNALS THE SAD END OF AN ERA IN BASEBALL

As he walked down the steps alongside his family, he saluted the fans with his hat.

The whole scene felt like something out of a movie – and a fitting end for one of the best pitchers of his generation.

Verlander, who was making just his second start of the year due to injury, still flashed a 95 mph fastball and struck out six Pirates hitters. His final career start was his first at Comerica Park in 3,324 days.

With Verlander riding off into the sunset, he also takes with him the era of the workhorse starting pitcher.

In addition to his MVP Award, he won three Cy Young Awards and a Triple Crown, was named Rookie of the Year, made 10 All-Star teams, won two ERA titles and is a two-time World Series champion.

Next for Verlander? Cooperstown.

item.title: Shaun Cassidy says teen idol fame trapped him before he made drastic career move at 21
item.description: Shaun Cassidy quit touring after his Astrodome show at 21, saying celebrity left him feeling like a prisoner and comparing it to Elvis' isolation.
item.content:encoded:
Shaun Cassidy had the screaming fans, the hit record and the television stardom. Then, at 21, he walked away from it all.

The former teen heartthrob revealed why he stopped touring at the height of his fame, saying the celebrity lifestyle had become less appealing than staying home, raising his children and creating television behind the scenes.

"I stopped touring when I was 21. Astrodome was my last show — not because I didn't love touring. I did, I loved performing, loved singing, but I found that writing and producing TV gave me, frankly, a much better life," he shared on the "Naked Lunch" podcast.

That decision came after Cassidy had already become one of the biggest teen stars of the late 1970s. His 1977 self-titled debut album spawned the No. 1 hit "Da Doo Ron Ron," while his role as Joe Hardy on ABC's "The Hardy Boys/Nancy Drew Mysteries" made him a familiar face in homes across America.

FORMER TEEN IDOL SHAUN CASSIDY CALLS OUT FATHER AS ‘PHONY’ AFTER GROWING UP ALONE IN HOLLYWOOD SPOTLIGHT

But Cassidy wasn't interested in spending the rest of his life inside the teen-idol machine.

"I got to stay home. I had kids at a young age. And I love writing," he said about his decision to give up touring.

For Cassidy, writing and producing offered something performing couldn't.

"I was a magician as a really young kid … when you write something, it's like magic. You pulled something out of the air and 200 people have a job on a sound stage."

FORMER TEEN IDOL SHAUN CASSIDY HAD TO RELEARN HIS OWN HITS FOR FIRST MAJOR TOUR IN 45 YEARS

By the mid-1990s, Cassidy had largely traded the stage for the writers' room and producer's chair, working on shows including "American Gothic," "Roar" and "New Amsterdam."

Cassidy said life as a teen idol left him feeling increasingly isolated.

He explained, "Because once you are well-known — at least in my case — I became insulated. I couldn't go out … kind of a prisoner in your house."

He added, "And that's one of the reasons again, like I don't want to be Elvis — not that I was Elvis, but you know what I mean — like I don't want that life. I don't want the Michael Jackson isolation, it's not healthy."

Instead, he said, he chose family and a life outside the glare of the spotlight.

"I'm glad I made the choice I did because now I've got a great life, I've got a great family, I've got … 107 children, and I'm a lucky man," Cassidy, who is father to seven children, laughed.

Cassidy's complicated relationship with fame began long before he became famous himself.

He grew up as the son of Broadway and television star Jack Cassidy and Oscar winner Shirley Jones, who became a television icon as Shirley Partridge on "The Partridge Family." Jack Cassidy and Jones married in 1956 and divorced in 1975.

Cassidy has previously described his late father as a "phony," saying Jack's larger-than-life showman persona didn't necessarily translate into fatherhood.

item.title: Maher blasts ‘intolerant left’ after Massachusetts lesbian bar faces fury for tweaking COVID-era mask policy
item.description: Comedian Bill Maher highlighted the struggling Last Ditch Bar, where lifting a COVID-era mask mandate one night a week sparked firebomb threats.
item.content:encoded:
Comedian Bill Maher took aim at his own side of the aisle Friday night, mocking far-left critics who torched a struggling Massachusetts lesbian bar for daring to go mask-optional one night a week.

During Friday’s episode of HBO’s "Real Time," Maher weighed in on the viral story regarding Last Ditch Bar and Arts Venue — a lesbian bar in Greenfield, Massachusetts that drew national headlines this week after the Boston Globe reported on a slew of community backlash surrounding the businesses’ decision to lift its COVID-era mask mandate for one night each week.

"Here's what's going on at the Last Ditch Bar," Maher said, adding, "It's a very woke bar, which is fine. Their mission statement [is], ‘For dykes, transsexuals, gender freaks, workers and friends.’"

NEWSOM'S ADMISSION THAT INFAMOUS COVID MOVE WAS 'INSANE' TRIGGERS VIRAL FURY: 'WE ALL TOLD YOU'

"I love the way workers and friends are fourth and fifth on the list," Maher joked. 

The comedian went on to delve into the bar's financial struggles. The Boston Globe reported that more patrons had said they could not afford the cover charge, and the bar allowed them in anyway.

MAHER SKEWERS WEALTHY CELEBS WHO PREACHED 'WE'RE ALL IN IT TOGETHER' DURING COVID AS AMERICANS STRUGGLED

"But economically, it wasn't working," Maher said. "Because even though there was a cover charge, if you couldn't pay, they wouldn't make you pay. Homeless, they were welcome in there. Not the cops, but the homeless. But also, it was masked"

Maher later pointed out that ‘because they're losing money, one of the owners was living in her truck."

BILL MAHER BREAKS WITH THE LEFT TO HAMMER ANTHONY FAUCI AFTER EXPLOSIVE SENATE HEARING

In an attempt to keep the doors open, Last Ditch made the decision to lift its strict KN-95 mask mandate one night each week — Saturdays — and allow patrons inside without the COVID-era face coverings, according to the Boston Globe.

"It is with love we inform our immunocompromised disabled divas we will be opening Saturday nights as mask optional," Last Ditch wrote in an Aug. 31 Instagram post.

‘COVID 2.0’: LAWMAKERS PUSH BACK ON SWEEPING HEALTH 'POLICE POWER' IN KEY BATTLEGROUND STATE

The backlash was swift, with locals flocking to a monthly community meeting on Sept. 11 to air their grievances, the outlet reported.

Virtual attendees were quick to criticize the bar owners for their decision, with the meeting taking another turn when some critics objected to a mediator, a licensed therapist who is White.

BILL MAHER BLAMES THE FAR-LEFT FOR PUSHING OUT LIBERALS LIKE JOE ROGAN, ELON MUSK OVER TO CONSERVATIVES

"A lot of people are calling for an acknowledgment of harm and I’m hearing a WHITE therapist … center[ing] the feelings of a majority white and white adjacent staff," one person said, the newspaper reported.

Maher took issue with the far-left bar patrons' apparent lack of understanding of the situation and blasted their intolerance toward the business.

BILL MAHER WARNS THAT THE DEMOCRATIC PARTY IS BEING 'COLONIZED' BY SOCIALISTS, SAYS HIS 'VOTE IS IN PLAY'

"And of course, the tolerant left did what they always do — became very intolerant and left," Maher said.

He went on to point to comments reportedly made by critics of the bar.

"And statements like, ‘People like you kill disabled people in the name of your own leisure and convenience,’ and ‘I hope your venue gets firebombed.’ This is what I'm talking about. This level of hatred that is out there."

Maher's criticism of the political left was noted by NewsBusters Executive Editor Tim Graham, who pointed out what he viewed as hypocrisy on both sides.

"This whole story went viral because it's shocking that a mask mandate is still in place at a bar in 2026. I imagine many people can feel more than a hint of the old COVID authoritarianism in the virulent leftist reaction to a single mask-optional night at this establishment," Graham told Fox News Digital. "These same people are probably furious at the Boston Globe for publishing this story. They don't care that the bar was a financial mess."

Graham added that Maher seems to have a pet peeve about liberals who preach tolerance but, in Maher's view, fail to practice it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"Bill Maher has a tendency to go against the dominant grain and can be savage about left-wing intolerance even though he was a massive supporter of Barack Obama," Graham said. "He's been very rough on organized religion, and can bring the pain to other strains of fundamentalism."

Fox News Digital reached out to Last Ditch Bar for comment.

Fox News Digital’s Landon Mion contributed to this report.

item.title: No. 1 Texas escapes Tennessee with thrilling SEC victory as President Trump watches on from Neyland Stadium
item.description: Texas silenced Neyland Stadium, as Colin Simmons recorded five sacks and Raleek Brown scored twice to beat Tennessee with President Donald Trump watching.
item.content:encoded:
It wasn’t pretty, but the No. 1 Texas Longhorns escaped Knoxville with its fourth win of the season against the No. 14 Tennessee Volunteers, 20-17. 

With President Donald Trump in attendance to watch this premier SEC matchup, Texas seemed to have the game in the bag when they went up 20-10 with 5:41 left to play in the fourth quarter. 

But Vols freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon, who was hounded all game long by the Longhorns’ defense, made things very interesting when he finally led a touchdown drive with less than two minutes to play. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Tennessee knew it needed some luck with no timeouts and only an onside kick recovery as the way they could win the game. If Texas secured the onside kick, Arch Manning would’ve knelt out the clock to victory. 

But the Vols, with a sold-out crowd at historic Neyland Stadium screaming, saw Texas receiver Ryan Wingo botch the recovery of the spinning ball. Brandon and the Vols’ offense got the ball back and had a chance to at least tie it with a field goal try and send the game to overtime, if not win it with a touchdown. 

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

However, Texas’ defense, as it was doing all game, put too much pressure on Brandon in the end. Brandon was sacked for the 10th time in the game, with Colin Simmons tallying half of those in a game where the Vols’ offense couldn’t move until the end. 

On the final play of the game, Brandon heaved a Hail Mary to the end zone, but Texas batted the potential game-winning ball away to secure its win.

This game ultimately matched the hype that surrounded it all week, especially after Trump's attendance was announced earlier in the week. 

Just after the national anthem, Air Force One flew right overhead, with the PA announcer at the stadium telling everyone to look up. A thunderous roar came from the crowd as the jet flew over, and the same occurred when Trump was shown on the big screen during a game break. 

With the president, and the rest of the nation watching, Manning and the Texas offense got to work early. On their opening drive, Manning found Emmett Mosley V on a 43-yard pass that set up the Longhorns beautifully on Tennessee’s 22-yard line. A few plays later, Raleek Brown burst through the line of scrimmage and picked up a nine-yard touchdown, capping a statement drive on the road to begin the game. 

From there, this game became a defensive bout on both sides. Tennessee would open their first drive with a field goal, but the score was just 10-3 at halftime as both defenses made it very tough for either quarterback to fall into a rhythm, especially Brandon making his debut against a SEC opponent. 

As the second half started, Tennessee knew that it had to get something to go their way, with the Knoxville crowd waiting anxiously to burst out in cheers. On Texas’ first drive of the half, that’s exactly what they got. 

After the Vols’ defense forced a three-and-out, Qua Moss caught a punt near midfield and took it 57 yards to the house to tie the game up at 10. Just like that, we had a game. 

The fourth quarter provided most of the thrill in this game once Brown scored his second touchdown of the game with less than six minutes left.

In the end, the Texas' defense came through when it needed most, even if it wasn't a smooth ride to get there.

item.title: Startups bring innovation to defense industrial base
item.description: Startups are helping modernize America’s defense industry with new technology and innovative ideas as the War Department diversifies its inventory.
item.content:encoded:
New tools, longstanding partnerships and additional resources could be the keys to bolster the defense industrial base.

The War Department is diversifying its inventory by working with startups and playing the long game through extended agreements with established contractors.

"I do think these are unprecedented deals," Undersecretary of War for Acquisitions and Sustainment Michael Duffey said. 

"Nobody's been able to deliver the quality and the performance that Tomahawk and the Patriot provide for our war fight."

The War Department has been announcing multi-year weapons production contracts. 

Some agreements extend as long as seven years, including a $22.9 billion deal with Raytheon for Tomahawk missiles, a $1 billion framework with Northrop Grumman and Lockheed Martin for THAAD components and a $58.62 billion contract with Lockheed Martin for Patriot Missile Segment Enhancements. 

INSIDE AMERICA'S LASER REVOLUTION AS THE MILITARY NEARS BIG BATTLEFIELD BREAKTHROUGH

"In the case of Patriots, it was a three-times production increase over what we were producing this past year," Duffey said. "We have a lot of new entrants that are bringing new great technology into the industry."

The War Department is also investing more in new technology. The Department of War Innovation Unit works with commercial companies and startups to adopt new weapons and defense capabilities. Its budget has skyrocketed to nearly $1 billion in recent years.  

"I think the startups are going to be kind of the future. The primes have their purpose. They build the big weapon systems. They build aircraft carriers. But it takes a long time to move that ship in the right direction," Rep. Michael McCaul, R-Texas, said. 

"The startups, just like we saw in Ukraine, have this ability of innovation to move at a faster speed and a more innovative technology, more creativity in the process, out-of-the-box thinking that we desperately need for our defense industrial base."

Rocket Lab is one newer company that has increasingly been working with the War Department. Since the company was founded in 2006, it has received more than $2 billion in government contract awards. 

"I would say we've moving up the food chain, and now we are amongst the preeminent missile and missile defense test programs in the United States," Vice President of Global Launch Services at Rocket Lab Brian Rogers said.

WAR DEPARTMENT OFFICIAL LAYS OUT PLAN TO REBUILD MUNITIONS STOCKPILE: 'AHEAD OF THIS PROBLEM'

Rocket Lab has worked with the Department of War Innovation Unit to test its Haste Launch Vehicle, which the company says will help the U.S. accelerate future hypersonic capabilities. 

"We've already done a number of launches," Rogers said. "We got a lot more in the hopper, and it's all kinds of different technology applications."

Defense technology company Castelion says one of its priorities is speeding up the manufacturing timeline.

"We believe that it's much faster if you just go out and build the object you're trying to build into inner manufacturing, and then you find all of the problems in that process, and you correct them," Castelion Co-Founder and CEO Bryon Hargis said. "One of the things that we based the company on is really what worked in the Apollo era when we got to the moon as a country in under a decade. A lot of those practices have fallen out of favor. We're going back to what worked, and we're just implementing that again."

The War Department is investing in that strategy with a multi-year agreement to eventually field Castelion’s Blackbeard Hypersonic Weapon.

"It's just the agreement to have a future agreement," Hargis said. "If we meet those performance targets that we set out and said we could do, the department is saying they're gonna come in and buy a tremendous amount of munitions."

Castelion has secured $500 million in U.S. military contracts over the past 18 months and recently announced $1 billion in funding. 

"The future is very bright. We have a tremendous opportunity with this administration and what the department is doing to bring in new entrants," Hargis said. "The key thing that I think has been missing in the past decades is that we do not build enough, we do not go test enough, and they're correcting that. And that's going to lead to tremendous innovation in this space."

item.title: Vicious bear mauls couple until their French bulldog intervenes with tragic consequences
item.description: A black bear mauled a Northern California couple at their Trinity County home, and their French bulldog Cassie died reportedly trying to protect them from the attack.
item.content:encoded:
A late-night encounter with a black bear turned tragic for a Northern California couple after the animal mauled the homeowners and fatally injured their French bulldog.

The dog reportedly tried to protect them during the vicious attack, which left them hospitalized.

In the early morning hours of Sept. 19, Jeff and Mallory Wilson's dog, Cassie, let out a single bark — prompting Jeff Wilson to go outside and check the backyard of their Trinity County home.

BLACK BEARS INVADE LAKE TAHOE HOMES AS BREAK-INS SURGE AND LOCALS FORTIFY DEFENSES

When he opened the door, a cinnamon-colored black bear emerged from behind their patio furniture, lunging at him and knocking him to the floor. 

The commotion woke his wife — who went outside and was then also attacked by the bear, according to a GoFundMe organized by a longtime friend of the married couple.

"I think the bear was startled by us just as much as we were startled by it," Wilson later told the news site Redheaded Blackbelt.

During the attack, their dog Cassie threw herself between Wilson and the bear, which grabbed the dog in its mouth and started to run away with it, according to reports. 

The owners got the bear to drop their dog and finally scared it off. 

GRIZZLY BEAR MAULS HIKER, DRAGS HIM DOZENS OF FEET ON GLACIER NATIONAL PARK TRAIL

Though badly wounded themselves, the couple rushed their dog to emergency care. The pet underwent surgery to treat multiple wounds, including along her spine — but "tragically died two days" after the incident, according to the fundraising page.

The page described the pet as "a deeply loved member of their family."

Jeff Wilson, meanwhile, suffered two broken ribs and numerous bite and claw wounds, while Mallory Wilson sustained serious injuries to her head and face, and other bite and puncture wounds. 

Each is facing continued medical treatment and recovery, the fundraising page says.

SAVAGE BEAR ATTACK LEAVES WOUNDED MONTANA HUNTER WITH HORRIFYING OPTION

The Wilsons own Radio Ranch, an off-the-grid "glamping" retreat in Trinity County, according to reports. The couple "[has] years of experience living and working alongside wildlife, and [takes] precautions to peacefully coexist with the animals that share their land," the GoFundMe notes.

"We chose to live in rural Northern California because we treasure being surrounded by the natural world and the wildlife with whom we share it," the couple told KRON4. 

"This was an unprovoked and extraordinarily unusual encounter that none of us could have anticipated."

"We can grieve Cassie and be devastated by what happened while still respecting the wild animals that belong in these places," they added.

"They are passionate animal lovers, which has made this extraordinarily rare encounter and the loss of Cassie heartbreaking on so many levels," the GoFundMe write-up noted. 

Jeff Wilson told local news outlets he believes the bear may have been startled after becoming cornered between a fence and gate at their home.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The attack has led the Wilsons to cancel Radio Ranch reservations while they recover and cooperate with an ongoing investigation by the California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW).

The fundraiser aims to help cover the couple's medical bills, veterinary costs, property damage and the expense of hiring help while they recover. 

As of Saturday afternoon, it raised over $16,000 of its $20,000 goal. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Fox News Digital reached out to the Wilsons and the GoFundMe organizer for comment.

The CDFW said black bear attacks that result in injuries to humans are rare in the state, the San Francisco Chronicle reported. 

The agency advises residents to secure food and garbage that can attract bears, keep pets indoors at night when possible and fight back rather than play dead if a black bear attacks.

The incident is the latest in several high-profile bear encounters this year, including black bear break-ins around California's Lake Tahoe region and separate grizzly attacks involving a hiker in Glacier National Park and a Montana hunter, as Fox News Digital previously reported.

item.title: Sharon Stone tells Sydney Sweeney to 'take responsibility' for provocative sports ad
item.description: Actress Sydney Sweeney's viral Novig ad drew criticism from "Euphoria" co-star Sharon Stone, who says women's sports shouldn't be denigrated.
item.content:encoded:
Actress Sydney Sweeney is taking heat from one of her newest co-stars on HBO’s "Euphoria" over her latest ad for sports prediction platform Novig that leaves little to the imagination.

"I think that it’s up to her to take responsibility for her actions, not up to me to judge her for her actions. It is up to me to be a cheerleader for the women who have made it through and become champions in women’s sports," Stone told the outlet.

SYDNEY SWEENEY LEAVES LITTLE TO THE IMAGINATION IN PROVOCATIVE NEW CAMPAIGN

"We can’t denigrate women’s sports to get men’s attention so they can gamble," she continued.

The ad depicts a nearly nude Sweeney posing in various provocative positions while holding sports equipment, with the actress telling viewers the platform lets them to bet on "just sports."

SYDNEY SWEENEY’S PROVOCATIVE SPORTS AD 'REINFORCES THE IMAGE SHE HAS ALREADY BUILT' DESPITE BACKLASH: EXPERT

The controversial video struck a chord with Stone, who told the outlet that while in high school, she threatened to sue administrators if she was not permitted to try out for the boys’ golf team, because her school did not have girls’ sports teams at the time.

"I had something to prove," Stone told PEOPLE, adding that she successfully "made the boys’ team."

Stone is not the first celebrity to take issue with Sweeney’s willingness to bare it all for the sports prediction platform, with numerous female athletes also taking to social media to voice their displeasure with her decision.

PUTIN UNLEASHES NEW FURY ON UKRAINE AS REPORT EXPOSES FEAR HANGING OVER WAR’S END

Russia alone has lost as many as 450,000 soldiers since invading Ukraine in 2022, according to the Center for Strategic & International Studies (CSIS).

item.content:encoded:

item.title: Someone could have opened an account in your name. Check now
item.description: New account fraud victims jumped 31% in 2025, reaching 5.4 million. Criminals open accounts you may never see on your regular bank statements.
item.content:encoded:
Most people think identity theft means someone gets into a bank account or starts charging things to a credit card you already use. But there is another kind of identity theft that can be much harder to spot. A criminal can use your name, Social Security number, birthdate or other personal information to open a brand-new account in your name. And this problem is growing fast. Javelin Strategy & Research found that the number of new-account fraud victims jumped 31% in 2025, rising from 4.2 million to 5.4 million. That was the sharpest increase among the fraud types Javelin tracked.

The fraudulent account could be a credit card sent to an address you have never lived at. It could be a phone or utility account with a company you have never used. Someone could even try to open a buy now, pay later account using your identity. That is what makes this kind of fraud so sneaky. The criminal may never touch an account you already monitor, so there may be no suspicious charge staring back at you from your bank statement. You may find out only when a strange bill arrives, a lender checks your credit, a debt collector calls or you spot an account that clearly does not belong to you. The good news is there are ways to look for those clues before the problem gets even bigger.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Get Better Healthcare With AI replay

Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed.

6 IN 10 IDENTITY CRIMES NOW BEGIN WITH A NEW ACCOUNT

With fraud on an account you already use, you have a decent chance of spotting it quickly. A strange purchase shows up, your bank sends an alert or your card suddenly stops working. New-account fraud can stay much quieter. A criminal applies for a new account using enough of your personal information to pose as you. If the application goes through, the account may be tied to an address, phone number or email account the criminal controls. As far as the lender or company knows, you opened it. The first clue could be a hard inquiry on your credit report, a new account you do not recognize or mail welcoming you to a service you never signed up for. But there is an important catch. Not every type of account appears on all three credit reports, and some phone, utility or buy now, pay later activity may not appear there. That is why checking your credit reports helps, but it should not be the only thing you watch.

Criminals have more stolen personal information to work with than ever. Years of data breaches have exposed names, Social Security numbers, birthdates, addresses, email addresses and other details that can help someone impersonate you. A criminal may also combine information from multiple breaches, phishing attacks or data broker records to build a much fuller picture of your identity. At the same time, opening financial and other accounts online has become incredibly convenient. You can apply from your couch and sometimes get a decision within minutes. That convenience works in our favor when we are the ones applying. It can also give criminals more opportunities to try stolen identities without ever walking into a bank or store. The Federal Reserve has also warned that digital account openings create new opportunities for fraudsters, especially as stolen personal information and more sophisticated technology become easier for criminals to use.

A criminal may not get everything needed to steal your identity from one breach. Your name and email could come from one leak. An older breach might expose other personal information. A people-search site may help fill in an address or phone number. Put enough pieces together and a criminal may have what they need to start testing your identity against lenders, retailers, phone carriers and other companies. That also helps explain why identity theft can seem to come out of nowhere. The information used against you may have been floating around for months or even years before someone decided to use it.

New-account fraud can leave clues in several places, and some of them are easy to miss if you do not know where to look.

You do not need to wait for a strange bill or collection call to find out something is wrong. A few quick checks can help you spot signs of new-account fraud before it turns into a bigger problem.

Go to AnnualCreditReport.com and review your Equifax, Experian and TransUnion reports. Free reports are currently available weekly, so you can check all three at once or stagger your reviews throughout the year.

Pay close attention to accounts, hard inquiries, addresses and other information you do not recognize. If something looks strange, do not assume it is harmless.

A credit freeze can make it much harder for someone to open a new credit account in your name because lenders generally cannot access your frozen credit report. Freezes are free to place and lift, they do not hurt your credit score and they stay in place until you remove them. You need to contact Equifax, Experian and TransUnion separately to freeze all three files.

Look for messages about accounts you never opened, especially welcome notices, bills, password-reset messages and application updates.

Your bank and credit card companies may offer account alerts at no charge. Identity theft monitoring can go further by watching for certain credit inquiries, new accounts and other signs that someone may be using your information. See my tips and best picks on Best Identity Theft Protection at Cyberguy.com . The faster you know something has changed, the faster you can investigate it.

IS YOUR SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER ON THE DARK WEB?

If you spot an account you do not recognize, act quickly. These six steps can help you shut down the fraud, limit the damage and start cleaning up your records.

Call the company's fraud department. Explain that you did not open the account and ask them to close or freeze it. Keep any confirmation they send you.

Go to IdentityTheft.gov and create an FTC Identity Theft Report and recovery plan. That report can also help when you dispute fraudulent information.

A fraud alert tells businesses to take extra steps to verify your identity before opening new credit. An initial fraud alert is free, lasts one year and requires you to contact only one of the three major credit bureaus. That bureau must notify the other two. A credit freeze goes further by restricting access to your credit report. To freeze all three reports, contact each bureau separately.

Contact any credit bureau showing the fraudulent account and ask it to block the identity-theft information from your report. To use the FTC's blocking process, send the bureau a copy of your FTC Identity Theft Report, proof of your identity and a letter identifying the fraudulent information. You can also dispute inaccurate information directly with the credit bureau.

Your bank and credit card companies may offer account alerts at no charge, so turn those on first. Identity theft monitoring can add another layer by watching for certain credit inquiries, newly opened accounts and other signs that someone may be using your personal information. That can be especially helpful with new-account fraud because the criminal may never touch the accounts you already check. See my tips and best picks on Best Identity Theft Protection at CyberGuy.com.

Write down who you contacted, when you contacted them and what they told you. Save letters, emails, case numbers and copies of anything you submit. Those records can save you a lot of frustration if you need to follow up later.

9 WARNING SIGNS OF IDENTITY THEFT YOU SHOULD NEVER IGNORE

New-account fraud can be especially tough to spot because the criminal may never touch the bank accounts or credit cards you already watch. That is exactly why I want you to check all three of your credit reports instead of waiting for a strange bill or collection call to show up. You can pull your reports for free, look for unfamiliar accounts or inquiries and consider freezing your credit when you are not applying for anything new. Then add alerts or identity monitoring if you want another set of eyes watching for activity you might otherwise miss. The big takeaway here is speed. A fraudulent account that sits unnoticed for months can turn into damaged credit, collections and a much bigger cleanup job. Catch it early and you have a far better chance of shutting it down before things snowball.

item.title: Trump's home county hits pause on data centers over environment and electric bill concerns
item.description: Palm Beach County passed a one-year moratorium on data centers amid concerns over environmental impact, noise pollution, and rising electric bills.
item.content:encoded:
Palm Beach County — home to President Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago — passed a one-year moratoriam on the planning and construction of data centers as commissioners seek to conduct a thorough review of data centers’ impacts on the environment, noise pollution, and electric bills.

The moratorium, passed on Thursday, comes just weeks after Trump said that communities that reject data centers would "end up being backwards and poor." Among the wealthiest counties in the country, Palm Beach County includes the town of Palm Beach, home to 65 billionaires.

"If you want to go through poverty, crime and squalor, I would say don’t approve of data centers," Trump said from the Oval Office on Sep. 4.

The Palm Beach County Commissioners’ 6-0 vote doesn’t put a permanent ban on data centers. Instead, it gives county leadership time to conduct environmental impact reviews before updating zoning rules for where data centers can be built.

TRUMP’S DATA CENTER PUSH FRACTURES CONGRESS AS LOCAL ANGER EXPLODES: 'GRASPING AT STRAWS'

The moratorium applies to all new applications for data centers with an anticipated peak electrical load of at least 50 megawatts.

"Many communities want the economic benefits a data center brings, but we all fear the higher power bills, the negative environmental impact, disruptive noise, the depletion of water resources," a Palm Beach County resident shared during Thursday’s meeting.

Trump has made expanding data centers and accelerating artificial intelligence a cornerstone of his agenda, arguing that the United States cannot afford to lose the AI race to China and warning that opposition to data centers only benefits Beijing.

Data centers are the physical backbone of artificial intelligence, housing thousands of powerful computers that store and process digital information while providing the computing power needed to train and run AI systems.

Palm Beach County has already approved in 2016 the construction of "Project Tango" — a proposed 202-acre AI data center, which is located 20 miles from Mar-a-Lago. The data center will also be built near an elementary school and homes.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS QUESTION WHETHER AI’S PROMISE OUTWEIGHS ITS RISKS

In July, commissioners voted 6-1 to reject a proposal to expand Project Tango by roughly 1.67 million square feet. But existing approvals for two 100,000-square-foot data center buildings remain in place.

Residents at the Thursday meeting said Project Tango was the driving factor behind the push to hit pause on data center project approvals, with several residents advocating for no data centers to be built.

"I think the best good neighbor data center is no data center," resident Sergei Kelly said. "We have the Everglades to our South and to our West. The coast to our East. I don’t think data centers, especially large data centers they want to build desperately should be here at all."

Fox News Digital reached to the White House and Palm Beach County Commissioners for comment.
